notes: The UK tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April.
If your income from self-employment is £1,000 or less in a tax year, the trading allowance may mean you don't need to tell HMRC.
Most sole traders count money when it is paid to them (the cash basis). Jobs not paid yet are shown on their own.
Online Self Assessment returns are usually due by 31 January after the tax year ends.
From 6 April 2026, Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies to sole traders with qualifying income over £50,000. It drops to over £30,000 from April 2027 and over £20,000 from April 2028.
This export is a record of your jobs. It is not a tax return. Check with HMRC or an accountant before you rely on it.
tax._note: Trading allowance £1,000 and MTD thresholds (£50k 2026, £30k 2027, £20k 2028) per GOV.UK as of 2026-10; recheck each April.
